newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling in rally vs dlr on coffee sales.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling in rally vs dlr on coffee sales.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling rallied against the dollar riding high on inflows from coffee export sales to levels last seen in June 1995, commercial bank dealers said on Thursday.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54 against the dollar compared to 54.26 on Wednesday. Against the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 87.75 from 88.18
"Most dealers were long dollars on Wednesday, and were offloading at almost price they could get," one dealer said.
"The market was extremely volatile. Rates dropped to 53.85/54.10 at Wednesday's close but appear to have steadied this morning," another dealer said.
"The central bank has kept off the market, and importers are sitting on the sidelines, watching to see how far down dollar rates will go," forex trader said.
The central bank's absence from the market this week has seen the shilling adjust itself against the dollar purely on market fundamentals, according to forex traders.
"With good reason they've supported the dollar in the past, for the sake of exporters who complain the shilling is too strong," one dealer said.
"But now with all the high foreign investor interest, all eyes are on the shilling to see at what levels it can stabilise without any interference," one dealer said.
They speculated that the bank appeared to face a dilemna of not wanting to appear to peg shilling/dollar rates versus protecting exporters' interests.
But, for the short term, market sentiment favors a stronger shilling, with the 54.00 level to be broken, they said.
The money market was slightly liquid with overnight rates quoted at 12 percent levels unchanged.
